title: v2 analysis output (analysis/stats.py -> results.json)
description: The document analysis/figures.py and analysis/table.py read, and the ONLY thing they read. Its central rule is that every numeric leaf wears the same envelope, so the plotting code never has to guess whether a number carries an interval, how many samples back it, or what units it is in. The other rule is that a quantity which was not measured appears as a null WITH A REASON, never as a zero and never as an absent key - a partial honest file is the goal, and a reader must be able to tell 'measured as zero' from 'not measured'. Conformance level: enforced by tests/test_v2_results.py against real analysis output, unlike schemas/benchmark_result.schema.json which describes a target the v1 path does not yet meet (see schemas/README.md).

_envelope_problems.description: Leaves that failed the envelope contract, recorded IN the document rather than raised: a run whose analysis found a contract violation still produced real measurements, and hiding the violation behind an exception would lose them. A non-empty array here means a figure drawn from this file may be wrong.

envelope.description: One numeric leaf. Exactly two legal shapes: a measured value with a unit, or a null with a short reason. Nothing else may appear where a number is expected.

ci95.description: [lower, upper] at 95%. Absent when the estimator declined to produce one - below three samples a resampling interval is an artifact of the samples, not a measurement of spread.

method.description: How the interval was built. Required reading before comparing two leaves: 'wilson' for proportions, 'bootstrap' for latency percentiles, 'normal' only for a mean, 'interval-arithmetic' for a ratio of two envelopes from different runs (conservative, wider than a joint bootstrap would be), 'single measurement' for a quantity measured once, 'datasheet' for a value that was never measured on this board at all.

row.description: One (config x condition) cell. Self-contained on purpose: the memory and quality blocks are repeated onto every row of a config so that figures.py never has to join two tables to draw a bar.

prompt_sha256.description: sha256 of the exact prompt string sent. The cross-framework byte-equality claim is checkable from this field alone: two rows from two frameworks that share it were sent identical bytes.

representation.description: The one-word precision label decomposed into the independent choices it bundles. Two frameworks' 'INT4' are not the same object, and this block is what lets a figure say so.

activations.description: A separate axis from weights, and not readable from the artifact - it is a property of how the runtime was launched, so it carries its own _source.

kv_cache.description: A third separate axis. It dominates at long context, where a per-token KV cost at 16 bits versus 8 decides whether a config fits at all.

calibration.description: Which data the quantizer saw, how much of it, and whether it resembles this deployment's domain. Null with a reason for an unquantized config or a vendor checkpoint whose publisher never said.

effective_bits_per_weight.description: artifact bytes / parameter count x 8. A bare number, not an envelope: it is an exact ratio of two counted quantities, not an estimate, so an interval would imply a spread that does not exist. The only field here comparable across all three runtimes without reference to the rest of the block.

comparability_class.description: Deliberately blunt, and never used to claim two configs in the same class ARE equivalent - only to mark cells where a direct comparison is not defensible at all. 'w4_grouped_mixed' exists because a GGUF K-quant leaves whole tensor families at 6 bits and is not the same object as a uniform grouped int4.
